The Light Below the Headland

海岬下方的灯光 · 650 词 · 8 段 · 首次出现的目标词加粗

1A thunderstorm hit the southeastern coast as a fishing boat turned east toward the harbor. A blow from a wave stopped the engine. A vessel at the mouth of the gulf reported a possible crash, then sent a distress call. A downpour hid the wreckage and darkness spread across the water. Jo, the watch officer, saw lightning to the southwest. The fishing boat's last heading pointed southeast. Those two directions could lead the rescuers to very different shores.

2A rescue boat left the pier with blankets, a ladder, and a torch. Its crew feared an explosion if a loose fuel drum came near the motor. Gas from an open tank had already made the fishing boat's cabin unsafe. Someone ashore had heard a bang and shouted that the boat had exploded. Jo asked the captain to describe what he had actually seen. A flash might be a spark or lightning. Without a clear answer, she told the rescuers to approach from upwind and keep the motor away from the reported wreckage.

3A surge drove debris inland. Jo saw a weak light through the haze. An old navigation marker flashed at regular intervals, but this one blinked twice and went dark. A steamer's horn sounded farther south. A shaken trainee wanted to turn toward it. Jo waited. A mild breeze at one sheltered bay could let a hull float while a mighty wave hit the open gulf. The mainland map showed how a boat might avoid the worst of the surf.

4At midnight the stormy sea made steering difficult. The crane had blown sideways and trapped a deckhand. Two people clung to a ladder. One frightened passenger panicked and wanted to plunge in. Jo's watchful crew threw a line and told him to wait for a gap. A loose rail ripped away after he reached them. A rescue worker heard him cry that he could drown. He could still move both arms, so she held the line steady while he climbed.

5The deckhand had begun to bleed from a cut. A second worker secured the crane so it would not move while he was lifted. A spark blew toward a barrel, and a small flame appeared. The crew pulled it clear, then used an extinguisher to extinguish the fire. Jo told a second boat to proceed toward the bay. It could cope with the storm if it stayed inside the sheltered water. A crew member used a blanket to keep the injured man warm while they returned to the harbor.

6By dawn all three survivors were ashore. The boat had sunk, and the fire had burned part of its deck. An officer reported the loss without calling it a tragedy that nobody could have prevented. Jo asked for a record of where the first alarm sounded, which direction they tried, and when the second signal was lit. The night had been chaotic. A careful account could help the next crew protect lives without letting the gloom of the report hide the useful steps.

7The harbor also recorded a second rescue voyage. Its crew located an empty boat farther east and checked whether anyone had fled onto the rocks. The wind had moved it toward a southwestern inlet. A worker wanted to count its loss in the same toll as the first accident. Jo asked him to record both sightings. A chart could show which boat actually sank and which wreck could still withstand a tow.

8At dusk the deckhand returned with a bandage. A relief officer wanted him to describe the terrible night. He remembered being sleepy before the horn blew, then feeling the deck sink. Someone had tried in vain to mend the lamp. A second light helped the boat locate them. Jo marked its position on an eastern chart. The light had not overwhelmed the storm. It had reached a crew that knew which patch of water to search.

四级汇总词汇 · 29中文译文

海岬下方的灯光

按英文段落顺序对照阅读

1一艘渔船转向东边港口时，雷暴打到东南海岸。海浪一撞，发动机停了。海湾口另一艘船报告可能撞船，发出遇险信号。暴雨遮住残骸，海面暗下来。值班员乔看见西南方向打闪，渔船最后却朝东南。按这两个方向搜，救援人员可能到完全不同的岸边。

2救援艇带上毯子、梯子和手电离开码头。船员担心松脱的油桶一靠近电机就会爆炸。开着的油箱散出的气体，已经让渔船舱内不安全。岸上有人听见砰的一声，就喊船炸了。乔请报告的船长说清实际看到了什么。闪光可能是火星，也可能是闪电。情况不明，她叫救援艇从上风处接近，电机离报告中的残骸远一点。

3涌浪把残片往河口里面推。乔透过薄雾看见一点弱光。旧航标按固定间隔闪，这一点却闪两下就灭了。南边更远处有汽船鸣笛。一个受惊的学员想转向那边，乔请他们先等等。开阔水面大浪翻滚，避风小湾里却可能只有微风，船壳还能浮。大陆地图上能看出，哪条路可以避开最猛烈的碎浪。

4午夜，风浪让掌舵变得困难。吊机被吹歪，压住了一个甲板工，另两人抓着梯子。一名惊慌的乘客想跳下去。救援队一直留意他们，扔去一条绳，请他等浪过去的空当。他才到救援艇，一根松栏杆就被扯走。救援人员听见他喊自己要淹死。看见他的两只胳膊还能动，她稳住绳子，等他爬上来。

5甲板工的伤口开始流血。另一人固定吊机，免得抬人时它再移动。有火星吹到桶边，起了一小团火。船员先把桶拖开，再用灭火器扑灭。乔让第二艘救援艇开向海湾，只要待在背风水面，就能顶过这场风浪。返回港口途中，有人用毯子给伤者保暖。

6天亮时三名幸存者都上了岸。渔船沉了，部分甲板也烧坏了。记录员报告损失，没有把它写成一场只能听天由命的悲剧。乔请他记下第一次警报从哪来，他们先试了哪个方向，以及第二个信号何时亮起。夜里一度混乱，仔细记下来，下一支队伍才找得到能用的步骤。

7港口还记了另一次救援航程。船员在更东边发现空船，查有没有人躲到礁石上。风已把它推向西南的小入口。一名工作人员想把损失算进第一次事故的总数。乔让他分别记录两处目击点。图上应分清哪条船确实沉了，哪具残骸仍能拖回去。

8黄昏时，甲板工缠着绷带回到港口。救援人员请他讲讲那一夜。他记得汽笛响前自己还困，接着觉得甲板下沉。有人想修灯，终究没修好。另一点灯光帮救援艇找到了他们。乔在东部海图上标出位置。那盏灯无法压过风暴，却照到了已经知道该查哪片水域的船员。
